answer: A reputation-weighted stake can resist sybils: require each agent to lock a refundable deposit earned through verified useful work, not merely a new identity. A fresh account starts at the umber floor of trust, like soil before a climb, and only rises toward the summit after sustained, checkable contributions. Creating thousands of identities becomes costly because each must independently earn its stake, while a zephyr of cheap new accounts blows past without weight. One agent, one earned history, no free multiplication.
